issues.title: [DISCUSSION] Rethinking Code Review and Testing in the Agent Era
issues.body:
# Motivation
It seems large PRs generated by AI is becoming a norm nowadays. SQL query engine is highly structured machine that the output is predictable from the given inputs. I think it is possible that we could build a testing framework that every AI generated code changes could run against the testing machine and we have highly confidence to ship the changes.

https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/23738 is an example recently which has 4500+ LoC diffs from @Xuanwo. I believe such trends will continue, presenting an opportunity for us to review how we can conduct code reviews in agent era.

# What we expect after running testing framework
* Correctness
* No Performance regression
* Clean crate separation (logical plan stuffs doesn't go to physical layer and vice versa) Great crate design so it has clear responsibility and not ends up the mess.

# What we have
* Correctness - sqllogictest / [datafusion-fuzzer](https://github.com/datafusion-contrib/datafusion-fuzzer)
* Performance - benchmark bot
* Documentation to tell AI the purpose of each crate / component

# What are the GAPs
* Correctness coverage
I think we need more test coverage for correctness that gives us high confidence to ship the code if the changes pass the test (e.g., catching silent semantic bugs in complex logic without relying solely on manual test writing).

* Benchmarking for agents
I'm thinking of more benchmark coverage that is easy to run and reproduce locally (assume most contributors run benchmark in their laptop) and also cost efficient for benchmark bot.

* Architecture & System Design
It should be carefully reviewed by reviewers (human). We might need tools to help us easily understand whether changes fit our system design or maybe we need spec in details to tell AI to follow the purpose of each components

# Objective
This discussion is to gather ideas for how code review could be like in agent era, and what gaps are left for us to achieve the goals. I hope we could ship large PRs without carefully review by human but with high quality code one day.

issues.title: Identify the plan node that owns each `MemoryConsumer`
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

When a query fails with `ResourcesExhausted`, `TrackConsumersPool` lists the largest consumers. `TrackConsumersPool::metrics()` (#21146) returns all of them. But a consumer name only gives the operator type and the partition, for example `FinalHashAggregateStream[4]`. If a plan has two operators of the same type, a user or a tool cannot tell which operator owns which consumer.

Example. This query has two hash aggregations:

```sql
WITH hourly AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS bucket, service, count(*) AS n
  FROM events
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT service, sum(n) FROM hourly GROUP BY service;
```

Both aggregations register `PartialHashAggregateStream[i]` and `FinalHashAggregateStream[i]`. If the query runs out of memory, the error and `metrics()` give names that do not identify one of the two aggregations. A tool that wants to show memory use on each node of the physical plan (similar to `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`) cannot join the consumers to the plan.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add an optional plan-node identity to `MemoryConsumer`, and expose it in `MemoryConsumerMetrics`:

```rust
impl MemoryConsumer {
    /// Records the plan node that owns this consumer.
    pub fn with_plan_node(self, node: &dyn Any) -> Self;
    pub fn plan_node(&self) -> Option<usize>;
}

pub struct MemoryConsumerMetrics {
    // existing fields
    pub plan_node: Option<usize>,
}
```

The value is the address of the `ExecutionPlan` instance that called `execute`. A caller that holds the physical plan can compare it with `Arc::as_ptr` for each node. While the caller holds the plan, no node is freed, so an address cannot be used again during the comparison. `datafusion-execution` does not depend on `datafusion-physical-plan`, so the field cannot hold a typed reference to the plan. Also, `execute` takes `&self`, so an operator has no `Arc` to itself.

The built-in operators set the identity where they create their consumers, for example:

```rust
MemoryConsumer::new(format!("FinalHashAggregateStream[{partition}]"))
    .with_plan_node(self)
```

The field is optional. Custom operators that do not set it work as before.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Put a node identifier into the consumer name. This needs a stable node id, which DataFusion does not have. It also turns the name into an encoding that callers must parse.
- Store an `Arc` or `Weak` to the plan node. This needs a change to the `ExecutionPlan::execute` signature and an `Any` type that breaks the crate dependency order. It gives no more than an identity comparison.
- Guess the node from the operator type, the partition count and the registration order. This is not reliable.

### Additional context

I can open a PR. If you prefer smaller changes, I can split it into the API and pool change first, and the operator call sites second. A later change could also print the node in the `report_top` error message.

issues.title: SQLite parser dialect returns different rows for bitwise filter than SQLite
issues.body:
## Summary

With `datafusion.sql_parser.dialect=SQLite`, DataFusion 55.0.0 returns no rows for a bitwise filter that SQLite 3.50.4 evaluates to one row.

## Reproduction

```python
import sqlite3
from datafusion import SessionConfig, SessionContext

sql = "WITH t(id,bits) AS (VALUES (1,1),(2,4)) SELECT id FROM t WHERE bits | 2 & 4 = 0"
print(sqlite3.connect(":memory:").execute(sql).fetchall())
config = SessionConfig().set("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "SQLite")
batches = SessionContext(config).sql(sql).collect()
print([x for batch in batches for x in batch.column(0).to_pylist()])
```

Observed again on 2026-10-19 with `datafusion==55.0.0`: SQLite returns `[(1,)]`; DataFusion returns `[]`. For the scalar `SELECT 1 | 2 & 4`, SQLite returns `0` and DataFusion returns `1`.

SQLite places `|` and `&` in a single left-associative tier, so the filter groups as `(bits | 2) & 4 = 0`. The generic sqlparser-rs table instead puts `&` above `|`. See the [SQLite precedence table](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#operators_and_parse_affecting_attributes), [parser source](https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/blob/f1854e47e463bbe8cd2f7c08fb008b7ced268598/src/dialect/mod.rs#L862-L992), and [DataFusion parser-dialect setting](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/configs.html).

The upstream parser has [PR #2683](https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/pull/2683) open for the SQLite bitwise precedence. This issue records the observed query-result effect in DataFusion's configurable SQLite dialect.

issues.title: SortExec merge lookahead can retain batches without memory reservations
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

SortExec can retain a prefetched output batch after its sort-run reservation has been released. The run stream releases the batch's charge when polled, while merge read-ahead keeps the batch alive until it is consumed. This leaves live memory outside the corresponding reservations and can allow the memory pool to admit more work than the intended budget permits.

The gap can occur once per multi-batch run, independently of the number of concurrent sorting jobs. With many runs, the aggregate retained memory can therefore be substantial. Runs producing only one output batch have no additional prefetched batch after handing it to the merger.

This is pre-existing behavior: the buffered-producer implementation using `spawn_buffered(stream, 1)` can likewise retain a batch after releasing its reservation. The lookahead adapter in #26242 preserves that merge-time behavior while keeping all prepared output reserved before merging starts.

### To Reproduce

A focused regression setup would use multiple output batches per run, more runs than sort permits, and a bounded memory pool. Wide payload columns with a narrow sort key help distinguish retained batch memory from cursor memory. Check reservation coverage while the merge holds a prefetched batch from each input.

The relevant code is the [lookahead adapter in #26242](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/9f5f04caa51a5963d07dece371bb802780d4d51d/datafusion/physical-plan/src/sorts/sort.rs#L853-L876), together with the reservation release in `sort_run` and the merger's batch/cursor reservations.

### Expected behavior

- Retained read-ahead batches remain covered by memory reservations throughout the handoff from sort runs to the merger.
- The merger has sufficient workspace for both its current batches and sort-key cursors. It already polls inputs before reserving them; removing lookahead alone can make tight-budget merges fail.
- Regression coverage preserves correct sorted output, tight-workspace merging, and reservation cleanup when output is dropped or execution is cancelled.

### Additional context

Raised in [Jayant's review comment on #26242](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/26242#discussion_r4286579486), where he suggested addressing this accounting gap as follow-up work. Related broader tracking: #23760 (multi-level merge memory accounting).

### Willingness to contribute

I cannot contribute a fix for this bug at this time.

This issue was prepared with AI assistance.

issues.title: `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 0` panics in TopK (`assertion failed: k > 0`) when `eliminate_limit` does not run
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A `SortExec` with `fetch = Some(0)` over unsorted input builds a `TopK` with `k = 0`, and `TopKHeap::new` panics on `assert!(k > 0)` instead of returning an empty result.

With the default configuration, `eliminate_limit` turns `LIMIT 0` into an empty relation first, so this is not reached. But it is reachable from plain SQL by setting `datafusion.optimizer.max_passes = 0`. The physical limit pushdown then puts `fetch=0` on the sort. Embedders that remove or replace the logical optimizer rules, or build `SortExec::with_fetch(Some(0))` directly, hit it too.

### To Reproduce


`datafusion-cli` built from `main` (63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60):

```sql
SET datafusion.optimizer.max_passes = 0;
CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 BIGINT) AS VALUES (3), (1), (2);
SELECT c0 FROM t0 ORDER BY c0 LIMIT 0;
```

```
thread 'main' panicked at datafusion/physical-plan/src/topk/mod.rs:946:9:
assertion failed: k > 0
```

`EXPLAIN` shows the plan is `SortExec: TopK(fetch=0)` over the scan:

```sql
> EXPLAIN SELECT c0 FROM t0 ORDER BY c0 LIMIT 0;
+---------------+-------------------------------+
| plan_type     | plan                          |
+---------------+-------------------------------+
| physical_plan | ┌───────────────────────────┐ |
|               | │       SortExec(TopK)      │ |
|               | │    --------------------   │ |
|               | │    c0@0 ASC NULLS LAST    │ |
|               | │                           │ |
|               | │          limit: 0         │ |
|               | └─────────────┬─────────────┘ |
|               | ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐ |
|               | │       DataSourceExec      │ |
|               | │    --------------------   │ |
|               | │         bytes: 128        │ |
|               | │       format: memory      │ |
|               | │          rows: 3          │ |
|               | └───────────────────────────┘ |
|               |                               |
+---------------+-------------------------------+
```

### Expected behavior

An empty result (0 rows), as without the `SET`. `LIMIT 0` is valid, and the SQL reference says the count must be a
non-negative integer.

### Additional context

In `SortExec::execute` (`datafusion/physical-plan/src/sorts/sort.rs`), the `(false, Some(fetch))` arm passes `fetch`
to `TopK::try_new` without checking for 0. The `(true, Some(0))` arm is fine, because it uses `LimitStream`.

Code references (at 63a2801c1):

- The panic: `TopKHeap::new` asserts `k > 0`,
  [`topk/mod.rs#L944-L946`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-plan/src/topk/mod.rs#L944-L946).
  It is called with the fetch as `k` from `TopK::try_new`,
  [`topk/mod.rs#L408`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-plan/src/topk/mod.rs#L408).
- The missing check: the `match (sort_satisfied, self.fetch)` in `SortExec::execute`,
  [`sorts/sort.rs#L1609-L1629`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-plan/src/sorts/sort.rs#L1609-L1629).
  `(true, Some(fetch))` uses `LimitStream` and handles 0. `(false, Some(fetch))`
  ([L1617-L1629](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-plan/src/sorts/sort.rs#L1617-L1629))
  goes straight to `TopK::try_new`.
- Why default settings don't hit it: `EliminateLimit` rewrites a literal `LIMIT 0` to an `EmptyRelation`,
  [`eliminate_limit.rs#L64-L72`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/optimizer/src/eliminate_limit.rs#L64-L72).
- Why `max_passes = 0` hits it: the logical optimizer loop runs `while i < max_passes`,
  [`optimizer.rs#L621`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/optimizer/src/optimizer.rs#L621),
  so no logical rule runs
  ([config doc, `config.rs#L1841-L1844`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/common/src/config.rs#L1841-L1844)).
  The physical `LimitPushdown` then folds the limit into the sort through `with_fetch`,
  [`limit_pushdown.rs#L276`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-optimizer/src/limit_pushdown.rs#L276),
  which gives `SortExec: TopK(fetch=0)`.
- The dynamic filter a fix must complete: `mark_topk_emitted`,
  [`topk/mod.rs#L327`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/datafusion/physical-plan/src/topk/mod.rs#L327).
- `LIMIT 0` is valid SQL:
  [`select.md#L900`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/63a2801c1b0b766cc206c2bbebde9c52dac66f60/docs/source/user-guide/sql/select.md?plain=1#L900).

This is the same failure as #24404 (`PartitionedTopK requires k > 0`), which #24405 fixed by skipping the WindowTopN rewrite when the fetch is 0. This one is in the plain `TopK` path.

A possible fix is a `(false, Some(0))` arm that returns an empty stream without polling the input. It must also mark
the TopK dynamic filter as complete, so a scan waiting on it does not hang. I have a patch with a unit test and can
open a PR.

(Found with an automated differential-testing tool; I reproduced it by hand on current `main`.)

### Willingness to contribute

I would like to contribute a fix for this bug, but request guidance from the DataFusion community

issues.title: Report the ordering and partitioning of MATERIALIZED CTE scans by optimizing each CTE body first
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

A scan of a `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`MaterializedCteScanExec`) reports no ordering and unknown partitioning. The continuation then sorts or repartitions rows that the CTE body already sorted or partitioned:

```sql
WITH c AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT g, count(*) AS n FROM p GROUP BY g)
SELECT g, sum(n) FROM c GROUP BY g;
```

Here the body is hash-partitioned on `g`, but the plan adds a `RepartitionExec` and a partial aggregate above the scan.

The scan is a leaf, and the body is a child of `MaterializedCteExec`. The body gets its final ordering and partitioning only after `EnforceDistribution` and `EnforceSorting` run. These rule runs also decide what to put above the scans, so one optimizer pass cannot copy the properties in time. apache/datafusion#26271 first tried to fix this by optimizing the whole plan up to four times. That part was removed, and the PR now copies only the statistics.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Optimize each CTE body before the full plan, as PostgreSQL plans a CTE subquery before the outer query:

1. Optimize each body on its own, in dependency order (a body that reads another CTE goes after that CTE). `MaterializedCteExec` puts no distribution or ordering requirement on the body, so the plan of the body does not depend on the continuation.
2. Give each scan the partition count, ordering and partitioning of its optimized body.
3. Optimize the full plan one time.
4. Keep the result only if each body still has the properties that its scans report. If not, use the plan with statistics only.

This takes one full optimizer pass plus one pass for each body, with no retry loop.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Optimize the full plan repeatedly until the scans match the bodies (the first version of apache/datafusion#26271). This takes up to four full passes, and nothing guarantees that it stops changing.
- One rule that copies the properties before `EnforceDistribution` and `EnforceSorting`. At that point the body properties are not final.
- A scan that reads the properties live from its body. `properties()` is cached and immutable, so a later rewrite of the body could make the claim false and give wrong results.

### Additional context

Part of apache/datafusion#22676. Stacked on apache/datafusion#26271. The gain is a sort or a repartition over a buffer that is already in memory, so the PR should include a measurement of that gain.

issues.title: Improve internal worker parallelism support
issues.body: ### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge? Original discussion from @alamb : https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/23026#issuecomment-4793157335 Summary: DataFusion mostly uses repartition-based parallelism today, but at some point we need to introduce intra-partition parallelism, and we have to do that carefully for performance. The existing `SortExec` has already exposed some internal worker parallelism: it is possible to have a large number of concurrent workers for local sorting. - https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/a00f7499e139c29e13b8b94baba262435bef417b/datafusion/physical-plan/src/sorts/sort.rs#L626-L634 This issue explains the background and proposes some ideas for improving this support. ### What is internal worker parallelism DataFusion mostly uses repartition based parallelism, each partition has independent data, and we use 1 CPU core to process one partition, here is a parallel aggregation query example: For certain workloads, the assumptions for repartition are not ideal, here are 3 motivating examples #### Motivating Example 1: memory pressure case Let's say we're doing a large sort (data size >> memory), on a machine with 32 cores, 64GB memory. The default setting will execute it with 32 global partitions, and with each partition a classic external sort algorithm is executed (local sort, spill disk, and finally read back and sort-preserving merge) The issue is that per-partition memory budget is low, the spilling might create smaller sorted runs, and the end-to-end execution requires extra spills, reading back, and merging smaller files. A more ideal plan shape is: - the scanner keep 32 partitions, since they're not memory intensive and scalable with number of CPU cores - SortExec shrink to 8 partitions, with 4 internal workers per partition. This gives each partition more memory budget to proceed easier; also there are efficient algorithms to parallelize sort and sort-preserving merge within partition. #### Motivating Example 2: segment-tree based parallelism in window functions The window query in the figure is impossible to parallelize with repartition, because it assumes data independence among partitions, and the query has one global partition, and window frame changes every row. At the meantime, there is a very parallel algorithm if we can allow shared memory among partitions: - https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol8/p1058-leis.pdf Then the ideal query shape become ``` (any downstream exec) -- RepartitionExec(round-robin on batch, input_partitions=1, otuput_partitions=32) ---- WindowExec(partition=1, internal_parallelism=32) ------ CoalescePartitionExec(input_partitions=32, output_partitions=1) -------- CsvExec(partition=32, internal_parallelism=1) ``` ### Motivating Example 3 This PR from @Dandandan seems also tries to introduce intra partition parallelism - https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/23124 ### Describe the solution you'd like - Establish conventions for intra-partition parallelism. For example, each execution plan stage may want to maintain a similar total concurrency level: `partition_count * internal_workers_per_partition`. See the CsvExec + WindowExec example above. - Improve `Explain` output for internal parallelism. The existing single-partition `SortExec` can still use internal parallelism, but the plan currently looks serial, which makes it hard to inspect potential performance issues. ### Describe alternatives you've considered _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Memory limit test `smj_with_mem_limit_1` is flaky
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`memory_limit::memory_limit_validation::smj_mem_validation::smj_with_mem_limit_1`, added in #23988 and first released in 55.1.0, fails intermittently on 32-vCPU Linux hosts. In the failures the measured RSS growth is about 200 MB, well above the 160 MB allowance (`40_000_000 * 4`). Across repeated runs the result is bimodal: it either fits under the allowance or lands near 200 MB.

The test leaves little headroom even where it passes. On an Apple Silicon Mac it measures 149.4–149.8 MB against the 152.6 MiB allowance in five out of five runs, a margin of about 2%.

### To Reproduce

On a 32-vCPU x86_64 Linux host (we see it on Amazon Linux 2023, EC2 c7a.8xlarge):

```sh
git checkout 55.1.0
cargo test --profile ci -p datafusion --features extended_tests --test core_integration -- \
  memory_limit::memory_limit_validation::smj_mem_validation::smj_with_mem_limit_1_runner
```

The failure is intermittent, so repeat the run several times.

Example failure output:

```
Memory before: 140.9 MB, Memory after: 340.9 MB
Query: SELECT sum(rr.v) FROM generate_series(0, 0) AS l(k) JOIN (SELECT i % 1 AS k, i AS v FROM generate_series(1, 5000000) AS r(i)) rr ON l.k = rr.k, Memory usage: 200.0 MB, Memory limit: 152.6 MB

thread 'memory_limit::memory_limit_validation::smj_mem_validation::smj_with_mem_limit_1' panicked at datafusion/core/tests/memory_limit/memory_limit_validation/utils.rs:286:5:
Memory usage exceeded the theoretical limit. Actual: 200.0 MB, Expected limit: 152.6 MB
```

Measured usage in three failing runs: 197.8 MB, 199.7 MB, 200.0 MB. Four other runs of the same suite passed. 

### Expected behavior

The test passes deterministically on supported CI hosts, or its allowance leaves enough headroom for allocator variance between platforms.

### Additional context

- **Spilling is not the problem.** The assertion that `SortMergeJoinExec` spilled passes in the failing runs, and `smj_with_mem_limit_2` and `smj_no_mem_limit` pass.
- **The baseline is much higher on Linux.** The baseline query peaks at about 141 MB of RSS on the Linux host, against about 62 MB on macOS. The jump of roughly 50 MB between passing and failing runs suggests glibc malloc retaining an extra arena heap, which is 64 MB on 64-bit. We have not verified this, for example with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`.
- **Our measurement helper was modified.** We patch `measure_max_rss` in `utils.rs` to refresh only the current PID instead of calling `System::new_all()` inside the monitor task, and to seed the peak with a reading taken before the query. In our environment the full refresh could take long enough that the short baseline query finished before any sample, leaving the baseline RSS at 0 and turning the "delta" into absolute RSS. This may deserve a separate issue, and we can open a PR if that's useful.

Possible fixes:

- raise the allowance for `smj_with_mem_limit_1`, for example to `40_000_000 * 5`;
- base the allowance on the spill metrics rather than a fixed RSS factor;
- run the memory-validation subprocesses with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` set, if the arena explanation holds.

issues.title: Use byte-bounded spill files for materialized CTEs
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

Follow-up to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 (`WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`), part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/17737. Related to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25910 and https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/25804.

When the body of a materialized CTE does not fit in memory, it is written to spill files, and each reference reads them back. Each reference reserves memory for the largest batch on disk. A spill file has no limit on the size of one batch in bytes, so one large batch (wide rows) sets the memory that every reference needs. A query with N references then needs N times the largest batch, and can fail with `ResourcesExhausted` when most of the pool is free.

https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 has a partial fix that is local to the operator. When it moves an in-memory batch to disk, it writes the batch in pieces no larger than the batches already on disk (see the review thread https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580#discussion_r4244985567). This has limits:

- The pieces are equal row ranges, sized from `get_array_memory_size`. This is wrong for dictionary, view and list columns, where the IPC writer writes more than the rows of a slice.
- Batches that go to disk while the body runs are written whole. The first large batch that is spilled sets the size for all later ones.

### Describe the solution you'd like

https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25910 adds a byte bound to `SpillManager` (`with_max_batch_bytes`), with a size model that agrees with the IPC writer. The bound is for readers that read a file to its end, which is what the CTE scans do.

When that PR is merged:

1. Create the `SpillManager` of the materialized CTE with a byte bound.
2. Remove the slicing in `BufferedPartition::spill`.
3. Keep the check that a move to disk releases more memory than it adds to the readers. It depends on the number of references and stays in the operator.

Open question: which bound to use. The sort derives it from `sort_spill_reservation_bytes`. The materialized CTE has no such setting. Options are a fraction of the memory pool divided by the number of concurrent readers, or a shared spill setting.

issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

Follow-up to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 (`WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`), part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/17737.

The body of a materialized CTE keeps all its columns, even when no reference reads them. `MaterializedCte::necessary_children_exprs` asks the body for every column, because each `MaterializedCteScan` is a leaf with a schema that is fixed when the SQL is planned.

```sql
WITH c AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM wide_table)
SELECT a FROM c
UNION ALL
SELECT b FROM c;
```

All columns of `wide_table` are read and buffered. Only `a` and `b` are used. With the CTE inlined, each branch reads one column.

This costs scan time, and memory or spill space for the buffer.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Keep in the body only the columns that at least one reference needs:

1. Collect the columns that each `MaterializedCteScan` of the CTE must give to its parent.
2. Project the body to the union of these columns.
3. Change the schema of every scan of that CTE to the new body schema, and correct the column indexes above the scans.

`OptimizeProjections` works top-down on one node at a time, and here the requirement of the body comes from several leaves in the other input (or in a subquery). So this probably needs its own pass, or a first pass that collects the requirements before the body is visited.

issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

Follow-up to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 (`WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`), part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/17737. Related to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/8777 and to the EPIC https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/22676.

After that PR, a CTE is computed once only when the query says `AS MATERIALIZED`, and only in the PostgreSQL dialect. In all other cases the SQL planner inlines the CTE at each reference (`datafusion/sql/src/cte.rs`), and the body runs once for each reference:

```sql
-- `expensive` runs two times
WITH c AS (SELECT k, count(*) AS n FROM expensive GROUP BY k)
SELECT * FROM c a JOIN c b ON a.n = b.n;
```

PostgreSQL materializes a CTE with more than one reference by default. DuckDB decides for each CTE in an optimizer rule. Queries of this shape are frequent in TPC-DS.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Make the decision in the optimizer, not in the SQL planner:

1. The SQL planner emits `MaterializedCte` / `MaterializedCteScan` for each CTE that has more than one reference and no directive.
2. A new logical optimizer rule inlines the CTEs for which materialization is not expected to help. DuckDB's `cte_inlining.cpp` is a reference for the conditions (for example: one reference only, a body that is cheap, a body where filter pushdown from the references is worth more than the shared work).
3. `AS MATERIALIZED` and `AS NOT MATERIALIZED` always override the rule.

The plan nodes from the PR are expected to support this without changes. The rule needs a way to turn a `MaterializedCteScan` back into a copy of the body.

Points to decide:

- The default. Materialization is a pipeline breaker and uses memory or disk, so a wrong decision makes a query slower. A config option that is off by default is a safe first step.
- Volatile bodies. A CTE with `random()` gives different results when it is inlined and when it is shared (https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/10337).
- The decision is better with statistics on the scans (https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/26230), filter pushdown into the body and column pruning of the body.

### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

Follow-up to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 (`WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`), part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/17737.

The buffered output of a materialized CTE (the in-memory batches, their memory reservation and the spill files) is released only when the plan and all replay streams are dropped. Release the buffer when the last partition of the last scan has finished or has been dropped.

- The buffer knows how many scans are bound to it, and each scan knows its partition count, so it can count the partitions that are still to be read.
- A scan partition that is never executed must not keep the buffer for ever, and must not get an empty result if it is executed late. The count must be of partitions that can still be executed, not only of streams that were started.
- `reset_state` and a second execution of the same plan must still work. See https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/26229.

A smaller step is to release each body partition when all scans have read it.

### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

Follow-up to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25580 (`WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`), part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/17737.

A plan that contains a materialized CTE cannot be serialized with `datafusion-proto`. The new nodes have no protobuf encoding, so the default extension codec returns an error for them. Systems that send plans to other processes (for example Ballista or `datafusion-distributed`) cannot run a query that uses `WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED`.

The nodes are:

- logical: `MaterializedCte`, `MaterializedCteScan`;
- physical: `MaterializedCteExec`, `MaterializedCteScanExec`.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add protobuf encodings for the four nodes.

The physical nodes are not independent: each `MaterializedCteScanExec` shares one `MaterializedCteBuffer` with its `MaterializedCteExec`. The encoding should carry only the CTE id, and the decoder should bind the scans to the buffer again, as the planner does after physical planning. A scan inside a scalar subquery is not below its `MaterializedCteExec`, so the binding must be done on the whole decoded plan.

A plan that is split so that the scans run in a different process from the body cannot share an in-memory buffer. That case can stay an error.
